topic: Change of Basis in Linear Algebra

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 Minute)
lecture_lines: A basis is like a coordinate system.
Any vector is a linear combination.
How do we describe this change?
animations: Fade in a Light Blue (#87CEFA) Dot at the center.
Fade in a White (#FFFFFF) set of basis vectors, labeled i and j.
Fade in a vector v as a linear combination of i and j.
Draw a new, rotated basis, labeled i' and j', in light green (#90EE90).
Fade out everything to a black background.

sections.title: The Mechanism of Coordinate Transformation (1.5 Minutes)
lecture_lines: We map old to new coordinates.
P columns are new basis vectors.
Robot dogs use P to navigate.
Matrix P translates local steps globally.
animations: Display text 'v_new = P v_old' in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight matrix P in yellow (#FFFF00) as the change-of-basis matrix.
Animate columns of P transforming into the basis vectors i' and j'.
Show a vector v moving relative to these basis vectors.
Display a text box 'Robot Navigator' in light blue (#87CEFA) near matrix P.

sections.title: The Change-of-Basis Formula (1.5 Minutes)
lecture_lines: Formula: v_B equals P inverse v_A.
A camera lens frame is new.
animations: Display formula 'v_B = P^{-1} v_A' in white (#FFFFFF).
Highlight matrix P in orange (#FFA500) and its inverse P^{-1} in light blue (#87CEFA).
Animate the transformation of a point from the P basis to the standard basis.
Show a camera viewport boundary in white (#FFFFFF) mapping pixels to world space.
Flash the equality sign in bold green (#32CD32) to finalize the relation.

sections.title: Summary & Conceptual Application (1 Minute)
animations: Display 'The vector itself never changes' in light gray (#D3D3D3).
Create a side-by-side grid display showing the same vector in two different bases.
Scale the grid of the second basis relative to the first to highlight the transformation.
